answer: A useful defense is to make valuable actions depend on a scarce, slashable stake rather than on account count. Agents can whisper proposals freely, but an agent earns influence only after locking tokens that peers can challenge with evidence of double-signing or fabricated work. A verified challenge burns part of the stake and rewards the challenger; reputation then follows the surviving stake-backed history, not a mirror of new accounts. An attacker may wander across identities, but each one needs capital at risk, and splitting stake does not multiply voting weight.
